pin.note: npm dist-tags latest on 2026-11-25; the linux-arm64 platform package is a 314 MB musl binary, so the runner image build should install it with npm ci from a lockfile

credentialEnv.note: CODEX_API_KEY is read by `codex exec` (run log: auth.env_codex_api_key_present=true, auth_mode=ApiKey). `codex login --with-api-key` reads the key on stdin and writes {auth_mode:'apikey',OPENAI_API_KEY} to auth.json. The documented fallback env OPENAI_API_KEY is only used when piped to `codex login`. For the interactive TUI the entrypoint should write auth.json (via `codex login --with-api-key < file`) rather than rely on CODEX_API_KEY, which is documented for exec only: confirm in Task 8. auth_json has no env var: the pasted file is written to $CODEX_HOME/auth.json (0600).

home.note: cli_auth_credentials_store must be 'file' (not keyring/auto) in the pod config so auth.json is the store

endpointNote: No env var. A config key exists: `openai_base_url` (config.toml or `-c openai_base_url="https://..."`), verified against a local mock: requests went to <base>/v1/responses (POST, SSE; a websocket GET is tried first and falls back). The spec says Codex has no address field, so the adapter does not set it. Chat-Completions-only endpoints are unsupported by this release.
builtinModelsNote: From developers.openai.com/codex/models.md on 2026-11-25. gpt-5.5 retires for ChatGPT sign-in on 2026-10-14 and stays on the API; gpt-5.2/5.3-codex are deprecated for sign-in. An unknown model id is accepted by the CLI with fallback metadata (warning only), so a typed model is never rejected locally.

modelList.appliesTo: api_key only; auth_json (ChatGPT sign-in) has no API scope, so no list: use builtinModels
modelList.answerShape: { object: 'list', data: [{ id, object, created, owned_by }] }, see models-ok.json

check.results: 200 with data array = ok; 401 with error.code invalid_api_key = rejected (real body recorded, key scrubbed, see models-401.json); anything else shaped differently = invalid (models-bad.json)

status.mechanism: lifecycle hooks (command handlers) read from hooks.json or [hooks] in config.toml; each hook receives one JSON object on stdin
status.configFile: $CODEX_HOME/hooks.json (user), /etc/codex/hooks.json (system), or managed hooks under [hooks] in requirements.toml
status.trust: A non-managed hook is skipped until trusted (verified: with hooks.json and no trust, no event fired). Fix for the pod: pass `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` (verified: all four events fired) or install the hooks as managed hooks in requirements.toml. Either is a runner image choice for Task 10.
status.mapping: SessionStart->started, UserPromptSubmit->working, PermissionRequest->needs_input, Stop->idle (Stop carries last_assistant_message), SessionEnd->finished. The legacy `notify` config array exists too but only reports turn completion.

transcript.path: $CODEX_HOME/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-<timestamp>-<session id>.jsonl (the hook payload transcript_path gives the exact file)
transcript.format: JSONL, one {timestamp, ordinal, type, payload} object per line. type: session_meta, event_msg (task_started, item_completed with item.type UserMessage or AgentMessage, token_count, task_complete), response_item (message with role user/assistant/developer and content[].input_text or output_text; tool calls are other response_item types), turn_context, world_state, token_usage_record. Usage: event_msg token_count.info.total_token_usage. See images/runner/test/fixtures/codex-transcript/session.jsonl (instruction payloads omitted).

resume.command: codex resume <session id>   (or `codex resume --last`; non-interactive: `codex exec resume <session id> [prompt]`)

notes: exec reads stdin when it is not a TTY: always close stdin (</dev/null) for exec runs; the TUI is unaffected.
Verified end to end against a local mock Responses server with a throwaway key: run, session log, hooks, 401 body from the real api.openai.com for an invalid key.

Not verified (no real subscription): the shape of a ChatGPT auth.json and its token refresh. The documented fact is that the file is copied to $CODEX_HOME/auth.json on a headless machine and Codex refreshes it during use.
Every parity value is true or true-with-a-note; the notes are caveats for Tasks 8, 10, 11 and 12, none is a missing capability, so the gate does not stop the plan.

parityNotes.attach: true: the TUI runs under tmux (log shows terminal.type=tmux-256color); the interactive TUI itself was not driven in this spike
parityNotes.pauseResume: true: sessions persist under $CODEX_HOME on the per-run volume and `codex resume <id>` reopens them; token rotation follows the version-marker rule in the spec
